messages:
Anya: Quick heads-up — noticed a small quality drift on fp8 canary this morning, ~0.8% top-1 drop on prompt set A.
Miguel: Ugh. Thanks for flagging. Which model + quant-profile?
Anya: gpt-small-v3 + fp8-v2. Canary was 10k reqs over 30m, sudden spike around 06:12 UTC.
Devon: @Anya can you paste the sample prompts that regressed? want to check for prompt-sensitivity.
Anya: Pasted a couple inline: 
```
"Summarize the policy document in 3 bullets." -> more hallucinations than before
"Translate the sentence preserving named entities" -> entity swaps occasionally
```
Miguel: deploy-bot shows canary rollout to 5% at 05:50, then to 25% at 06:00. runtime-bot: traces show an increased token error rate on attention kernels for longctx.
runtime-bot: Canary deploy started: fp8-v2 on inference-prod (canary=25%).
Shreya: Is this marginal or something we'd expect from fp8 quant noise? 0.8% seems small but could matter for some SLAs.
Samir: We should differentiate: statistical wobble vs systematic bias. Is drop concentrated on a subset of prompts?
Anya: It's concentrated on prompts with long entity lists + numbers. Short conversational queries are fine.
Devon: That suggests quant noise on attention normalization or MLP scaling. Could be headwise scale mismatch.
Miguel: Suggest we run a focused A/B: route 1k requests from the failing prompt slice to both fp8-v2 and baseline fp16 and compute per-prompt degradation. If consistent, rollback.
Shreya: Ops concern: how do we surface this in Console so oncall can act without engineering deep-dive? We need clear canary criteria.
Miguel: Proposed canary failure criteria (draft):
```
{
  "duration": "30m",
  "min_requests": 1000,
  "quality_delta_threshold": 0.5, // percent
  "slice_failure_rate": 0.05 // fraction of prompt slices exceeding the delta
}
```
Samir: +1 but add an absolute metric floor (e.g., top-1 accuracy must be >= 93%) and a per-slice minimum sample count to avoid noisy slices.
Anya: Also add a telemetry sampling tweak: increase shadow sampling for suspected slices so we get more signal without full traffic shift.
Devon: Operational UX question: how do devs annotate slices? Manual tagging is slow. We should support automated slice definitions derived from eval labels and runtime features (longctx, numeric-heavy, named-entity count).
Shreya: Agree. In Console show a "danger slice" banner when a slice's pctl drop > threshold and sample_count > min. Include quick rollback button on the rollout panel.
Miguel: For runtime safety nets: if latency also spikes with quant variant (we've seen kernel thrash on mixed-precision), fallback to cpu fp16 path for that request class. runtime-bot: note — fallback adds ~40ms p95 but preserves quality.
Samir: We need better telemetry for quant-specific signals: per-head activation norms, MLP scale drift, sign-flip counters. Those should be cheap to compute (sampled) and exposed in the precision dashboard.
Anya: Logged a follow-up ticket: link to regression repro + sample prompts. Tagging @Devon @Miguel for triage.
Devon: I'll slot a short experiment to run targeted A/B and add extra shadow logs for the failing slice. Can we get a temporary high-sample shadow stream?
Shreya: Ops can enable it for 1 hour during low traffic window. Need a one-click toggle in Console (can we?)
Miguel: We should design a small "quant-canary" manifest that teams can reuse. Minimal fields: model, quant_profile, slices, thresholds, shadow_sampling, rollback_policy. Example:
```
quant_canary:
  model: gpt-small-v3
  quant_profile: fp8-v2
  slices:
    - name: long_entities
      filter: "named_entity_count > 3 and token_count > 80"
  thresholds:
    quality_delta_pct: 0.5
    min_samples: 100
  shadow_sampling: 0.2
  rollback_policy: immediate_if_slice_violation
```
Samir: That manifest looks good. Add an opt-in field for per-head diagnostics to reduce default overhead.
Anya: TL;DR ops asks: 1) add canary manifest + one-click shadow toggle; 2) expose slice-level banners + rollback; 3) telemetry for quant signals.
Miguel: I'll draft a follow-up RFC for API + runtime hooks for the manifest and diagnostics. Will include cost estimate for extra sensors.
Devon: If we hit persistent regressions, we should also support automatic fallback to a slightly higher-precision profile (e.g., fp8-v2 -> int8-mixed or fp16-warm) for slices where quality matters.
Shreya: Agree; but add guardrails so customers can opt-out for deterministic latency.
Anya: Thanks team. For now ops will pause canary at 25% and enable focused A/B. Will update thread with results. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Canary pause executed at 06:14 UTC (canary=25% -> hold).
runtime-bot: Shadow sampling ramped to 0.5 for slice long_entities (1h window).
Samir: Moving to follow-up PRs: dashboard banners, canary manifest schema, and a lightweight diagnostics flag.
Miguel: Sounds good. Capture action items and owners?
Anya: Actions: Miguel RFC + manifest (ETA 72h), Devon A/B job + logs (ETA 24h), Shreya Ops UI quick toggle (ETA 48h), Samir telemetry sensors (ETA 5d).
Shreya: I'll create an ops runbook entry for quant-canary failures.
Anya: Closing for now — will post results here.
